Tuesday, 1 am. Rewrote Sumeet's login code again after everyone left. Third time this month. The deadline is Friday, there's no time to explain, and explaining would take longer than just doing it. Sumeet doesn't know. He'll send the next ticket and we'll go around again. My neck aches and my eyes burn. Tomorrow I have to sit at stand-up and act as though everything's fine. I keep thinking he'll never learn what was wrong, because I've never told him. Maybe I should have said something in week one. Maybe next week. I can't see how long I can keep this up, and the code he writes hasn't changed at all.

Rukmini

qa.a: It is the third time this month.

qa.q: How does Rukmini feel at 1 am after the rewrite?
qa.a: Rukmini feels exhausted and anxious, with an aching neck and burning eyes, and unsure how long this can continue.

qa.q: What could Rukmini do differently, and why?
qa.a: Rukmini could show Sumeet the changes in daytime and explain the reasons, because he cannot improve at what he never gets told about.

qa.q: How might Sumeet see the situation?
qa.a: Sumeet probably thinks the code is fine, since nobody has told him otherwise, and he does not know how much extra work Rukmini is doing.

grounding: Illustrates a lead rewriting a junior's code at night without telling him to meet deadlines, so he never learns and the lead burns out.

Nandita: I'm so tired. I fell asleep in the standup yesterday
(three weeks later)

qa.q: What would you change first in Nandita's approach?

subtype: Approach: doing the junior's work quietly [Pitfall]
passage:
Simran ran the small accounts team at the rice mill office outside Karnal. Every evening she stayed back after everyone left, redoing the ledger entries Gopal, the new junior, had made that day.
"Why are you so late again?" her sister Rashmi asked when she came home at ten, dal already cold.
"Gopal's entries have errors. The audit is next month. It's quicker if I fix them myself."
"Does he know?"
Simran shook her head. "He'd feel bad."
Two months later, Gopal's entries still had the same errors in the same columns. He had no idea anything was wrong; his work always seemed to come back fine. Simran had dark circles under her eyes and snapped at her mother over nothing.
One night, Rashmi found her asleep at the table with the ledger open.
"Didi, this isn't helping him either," she said softly.

qa.q: What time did Simran come home?
Why didn't Simran tell Gopal about his errors?
qa.a: She was worried he would feel bad, and she wanted to avoid an awkward talk, even though fixing them herself was wearing her out.

qa.q: What else could Simran try instead of fixing the entries herself?
qa.a: She could go through one day's errors with Gopal, show him the pattern, and check his entries together briefly each evening until he improves.

qa.q: How does Simran's approach look to Rashmi?
qa.a: Rashmi watches her sister come home late and exhausted and sees that the quiet fixing isn't helping Gopal either, so she is worried.

grounding: It shows a lead quietly redoing a junior's work to meet deadlines, so he never learns his mistakes and she wears herself out while his work stays the same.
